title: Write Equations
contentObjective: I can write an equation to represent a real-world situation.
languageObjective: I can explain my equation using the words equation, variable, equal sign, and expression.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Locker Clue
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Ruiz finds a clue at a crime scene: 'A number of suspect's stolen coins, plus 7 more coins found in a locker, equals 31 coins in all.' Let c stand for the number of stolen coins. Write an equation that represents this clue, then find how many coins were stolen.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Equation: c + 7 = 31. Since c = 31 − 7 = 24, the suspect stole 24 coins.

turnAndTalk.question: Detective Ruiz's clue says 'a number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' How would you turn this clue into an equation, and what does each part stand for?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I let a variable stand for the unknown number of gems.

stems.en: The unknown is ___, so I write the variable ___.
stems.es: La incógnita es ___, así que escribo la variable ___.

stems.en: My equation is ___ because 'plus 8' means ___ and 'equals 20' means ___.
stems.es: Mi ecuación es ___ porque 'más 8' significa ___ y 'es igual a 20' significa ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students choose a variable (such as n) for the unknown gems, build n + 8 = 20, and connect 'plus 8 more' to + 8 and 'equals 20 total' to = 20.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why does the equation n + 8 = 20 represent the clue better than the expression n + 8 alone? Justify using the role of the equal sign.
extendStems: The equation is better than the expression because ___.
The equal sign tells me ___ that an expression cannot show.

turnAndTalk.question: On the balance scale you put n + 8 on one side and 20 on the other. How did you decide what belongs on each side of the equal sign?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Both sides of the equation must represent the same total.

stems.en: I put ___ on the left side because ___.
stems.es: Puse ___ en el lado izquierdo porque ___.

stems.en: The equal sign means both sides are ___.
stems.es: El signo igual significa que ambos lados son ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students place the expression n + 8 on one side and the total 20 on the other, explaining the equal sign means both sides have the same value.
turnAndTalk.extend: Compare 'twice a number equals 20' with 'a number plus 8 equals 20.' How would the equations differ, and why?
extendStems: 'Twice a number' would be ___ instead of ___ because ___.
The operation changes the equation because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When would writing an equation help you solve a real problem instead of just guessing?
turnAndTalk.kernel: An equation organizes what I know and what I want to find.

stems.en: Writing an equation helps me because ___.
stems.es: Escribir una ecuación me ayuda porque ___.

stems.en: I would write an equation to find ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students explain that an equation captures the relationship clearly, lets you use a variable for the unknown, and can be solved instead of guessing.
turnAndTalk.extend: Critique: 'Any sentence with numbers is an equation.' Use the words expression and equal sign to explain why this is wrong.
extendStems: This is wrong because an expression ___.
A sentence is only an equation when it has ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Write Equations, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign.

stems.en: I put ___ on the left side because ___.
stems.es: Puse ___ en el lado izquierdo porque ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.8 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con un signo igual que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: A math sentence that says two amounts are equal, with an = sign, is an ___.

That is an expression because it has no equal sign.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una letra que representa un número desconocido o que puede cambiar.
vocabulary.visual: In n + 3 = 10, the letter n stands for the unknown number (n = 7)

conceptIntro.heading: How do I turn a word clue into an equation?
conceptIntro.intro: An equation is a math sentence with an equal sign (=). To write one, I pick a letter (a variable) for the unknown number and match the words to math symbols.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign.

The unknown is the number of gems. I let n stand for it.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: New clue: 'A number plus 5 equals 9.' What is the unknown?
We let n be the unknown. What does 'plus 5' tell us to write?
What does 'equals 9' tell us? Put it together: n + 5 = 9.

explore.instructions: Use the balance scale to see how each word problem translates into an equation. Drag the correct expression to each side of the scale to make it balance.
hints: Read the situation: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' The unknown is the number of stolen gems — that's n.
The left side is n + 8 (gems plus 8 more). The right side is 20 (the total). Balance them: n + 8 = 20.
explore.label: Build the equation on the balance scale. What goes on each side?

discourse.prompt: How did you decide what expression to put on each side of the balance?
discourse.sentenceFrame: I put ___ on the left side because ___, and ___ on the right side because ___. The equal sign means ___.

diagram.intro: Now write the solving steps on paper-style lines — I'll check each one keeps the same solution.

optional.stem: A witness statement reads: 'A number c of security cameras plus 6 more equals 19.' Which equation matches?
optional.explanation: 'Plus 6 more' means + 6 and 'equals 19' means = 19, so c + 6 = 19. Check: 13 + 6 = 19.
choiceFeedback: Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
That shows removing 6. The words say plus 6.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
optional.stemEs: Una declaración de un testigo dice: 'Un número c de cámaras de seguridad más 6 más es igual a 19.' ¿Cuál ecuación corresponde?
optional.explanationEs: 'Más 6 más' significa + 6 y 'es igual a 19' significa = 19, así que c + 6 = 19. Comprueba: 13 + 6 = 19.
hints: An equation matches the words piece by piece: a starting amount, an operation, and what the total equals.
Name the unknown first — c is the number of cameras you do not know yet — then translate 'plus 6 more' into an operation.
Begin writing it: c comes first, then the operation for 'plus 6 more', then the equals sign with 19. Pick the operation the words describe.
hintsEs: Una ecuación corresponde a las palabras parte por parte: una cantidad inicial, una operación y a cuánto es igual el total.
Nombra primero la incógnita: c es el número de cámaras que aún no conoces. Luego traduce 'más 6 más' a una operación.
Empieza a escribirla: primero va c, luego la operación de 'más 6 más', y después el signo igual con 19. Elige la operación que describen las palabras.

optional.stem: The lab tech says: '5 times the number of evidence bags b equals 35.' Which equation represents this clue?
optional.explanation: '5 times the number' means 5 times b, so 5b = 35. Check: 5 × 7 = 35.
choiceFeedback: "Times" means multiply, not add.
That shows subtracting 5. The words say 5 times.
"Times" means multiply, not divide.
optional.stemEs: El técnico del laboratorio dice: '5 veces el número de bolsas de evidencia b es igual a 35.' ¿Cuál ecuación representa esta pista?
optional.explanationEs: '5 veces el número' significa 5 por b, así que 5b = 35. Comprueba: 5 × 7 = 35.
hints: Words like 'times' tell you exactly which operation belongs in the equation.
The unknown is b, the number of evidence bags, and the clue says that amount is repeated a certain number of times.
'5 times b' is written by putting the 5 directly in front of b. Set that expression equal to 35 and see which choice matches.
hintsEs: Palabras como 'veces' te dicen exactamente qué operación va en la ecuación.
La incógnita es b, el número de bolsas de evidencia, y la pista dice que esa cantidad se repite cierto número de veces.
'5 veces b' se escribe poniendo el 5 justo delante de b. Iguala esa expresión a 35 y observa cuál opción coincide.

optional.stem: A torn note reads: 'A suspect's case minutes m, after 9 fewer, leaves 24.' Which equation fits?
optional.explanation: '9 fewer' means subtract 9, so m − 9 = 24. Check: 33 − 9 = 24.
choiceFeedback: The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Subtraction is needed here, not multiplication.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
optional.stemEs: Una nota rota dice: 'Los minutos m del caso de un sospechoso, después de 9 menos, dejan 24.' ¿Cuál ecuación corresponde?
optional.explanationEs: '9 menos' significa restar 9, así que m − 9 = 24. Comprueba: 33 − 9 = 24.
hints: Read the words in the order the amount changes: something started, something was taken away, and something was left.
'9 fewer' means 9 are removed from the starting amount m, not the other way around.
Start with m, then take away the 9 that were lost, and set the result equal to what remains.
hintsEs: Lee las palabras en el orden en que cambia la cantidad: algo empezó, algo se quitó y algo quedó.
'9 menos' significa que se quitan 9 de la cantidad inicial m, no al revés.
Empieza con m, quita los 9 que se perdieron e iguala el resultado a lo que queda.

optional.label: Match each detective clue to the equation that cracks it.

pairs.term: A number d of door codes plus 4 equals 17.
6 times the number of tips t equals 42.
A pile of files f, after losing 11, equals 20.
A number of suspects s split into 5 vans equals 8 per van.

optional.hint: Read each item carefully, then match based on what the problem is asking.
optional.explanation: Each clue names its variable and one action, which fixes the equation: adding 4 to d gives d + 4 = 17, six groups of t gives 6t = 42, losing 11 from f gives f − 11 = 20, and splitting s into 5 vans gives s / 5 = 8. Reading the action word — plus, times, losing, split — is enough to identify each match.
optional.explanationEs: Cada pista nombra su variable y una acción, y eso fija la ecuación: sumar 4 a d da d + 4 = 17, seis grupos de t dan 6t = 42, perder 11 de f da f − 11 = 20, y repartir s en 5 camionetas da s / 5 = 8. Leer la palabra de acción —más, veces, perder, repartir— basta para identificar cada pareja.
optional.labelEs: Une cada pista del detective con la ecuación que la resuelve.

optional.instructions: Drag each clue phrase into the operation a detective should write.
optional.hint: Sort by the key operation or concept each item shows.
optional.explanation: 'Increased by 7' and 'sum of clues' both grow the amount, so they are addition, while '13 fewer than' and 'decreased by 8' both shrink it, so they are subtraction. 'Triple the tips' means three equal copies, which is multiplication, and 'split equally among' shares one amount into equal groups, which is division.
optional.explanationEs: 'Increased by 7' y 'sum of clues' aumentan la cantidad, así que son suma, mientras que '13 fewer than' y 'decreased by 8' la reducen, así que son resta. 'Triple the tips' significa tres copias iguales, lo cual es multiplicación, y 'split equally among' reparte una cantidad en grupos iguales, lo cual es división.
optional.instructionsEs: Arrastra cada frase de pista a la operación que debería escribir un detective.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Crack the Detective's Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: A number of footprints divided by 4 equals 6.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let f represent the number of footprints.

optional.correctWork: 'Divided by 4' means division, not multiplication. The correct equation is f / 4 = 6. Check: 24 / 4 = 6.
hints: Reread the clue: does 'divided by 4' mean you multiply by 4 or split into 4?
'Divided by 4' is f / 4, so the equation is f / 4 = 6, not 4f = 6.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Descifra el error del detective
optional.explanation: Choosing f for the footprints was fine, but the equation 4f = 6 turns the division into a multiplication. 'Divided by 4' means f is split into 4 equal groups, so the equation is f / 4 = 6, and 24 / 4 = 6 confirms it.
optional.explanationEs: Elegir f para las huellas estuvo bien, pero la ecuación 4f = 6 convierte la división en una multiplicación. 'Dividido entre 4' significa que f se reparte en 4 grupos iguales, así que la ecuación es f / 4 = 6, y 24 / 4 = 6 lo confirma.

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number plus 12 equals 30'?
approaching.explanation: 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + ___ = ___.
Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
hints: Find the operation word in the sentence. What does 'plus' tell you to do with the number and 12?
Let n stand for the unknown number, then translate each phrase into symbols: 'a number' becomes n, 'plus 12' names an operation, 'equals 30' becomes = 30.
Build it left to right: n, then the symbol for 'plus', then 12, then '= 30'. Which choice matches that exact order?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Un número más 12 es igual a 30'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Más' significa suma, así que la ecuación es n + 12 = 30.
hintsEs: Halla la palabra de operación en la oración. ¿Qué te dice 'más' que hagas con el número y el 12?
Deja que n represente el número desconocido y luego traduce cada frase a símbolos: 'un número' se vuelve n, 'más 12' nombra una operación y 'es igual a 30' se vuelve = 30.
Ármalo de izquierda a derecha: n, luego el símbolo de 'más', luego 12, luego '= 30'. ¿Qué opción coincide con ese orden exacto?

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'Seven less than a number is 18'?
approaching.explanation: 'Seven less than a number' means start with the number and subtract 7: n − 7 = 18.
choiceFeedback: Start with the variable, then subtract — not the other way.
The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
hints: 'Seven less than a number' is tricky — the number comes FIRST, and then 7 is taken away from it.
'Less than' flips the wording: '7 less than n' means start at n and subtract 7, not start at 7 and subtract n.
Write the number first: n, then subtract 7, then set it equal to 18. Which choice is built in that order?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Siete menos que un número es 18'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Siete menos que un número' significa empezar con el número y restar 7: n − 7 = 18.
hintsEs: 'Siete menos que un número' es tramposo: el número va PRIMERO y luego se le quitan 7.
'Menos que' invierte el enunciado: '7 menos que n' significa empezar en n y restar 7, no empezar en 7 y restar n.
Escribe el número primero: n, luego resta 7 y luego iguálalo a 18. ¿Qué opción está armada en ese orden?

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'Three times a number equals 21'?
approaching.explanation: 'Three times' means multiply by 3, so the equation is 3n = 21.
choiceFeedback: "Times" means multiply, not add.
That shows subtracting 3. The words say three times.
"Times" means multiply, not divide.
hints: Circle the operation word: 'times'. What operation does 'times' always signal?
'Three times a number' means 3 multiplied by n, written 3n with no symbol between the 3 and the n.
Put 3n on the left and set it equal to 21. Which choice shows multiplication instead of adding or subtracting 3?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Tres veces un número es igual a 21'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Tres veces' significa multiplicar por 3, así que la ecuación es 3n = 21.
hintsEs: Encierra la palabra de operación: 'veces'. ¿Qué operación señala siempre 'veces'?
'Tres veces un número' significa 3 multiplicado por n, y se escribe 3n sin ningún símbolo entre el 3 y la n.
Pon 3n a la izquierda e iguálalo a 21. ¿Qué opción muestra multiplicación en vez de sumar o restar 3?

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number divided by 4 equals 8'?
choiceFeedback: "Divided" means division, not multiplication.
That shows subtracting 4. The words say divided by 4.
Use division here, not addition.
hints: The phrase 'divided by 4' names the operation. Which symbol shows division?
Keep the sentence order: the number n comes first, THEN it gets divided by 4.
Write n, then the division symbol, then 4 on the left side, and '= 8' on the right. Which choice matches exactly?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Un número dividido entre 4 es igual a 8'?
hintsEs: La frase 'dividido entre 4' nombra la operación. ¿Qué símbolo muestra división?
Conserva el orden de la oración: el número n va primero y DESPUÉS se divide entre 4.
Escribe n, luego el símbolo de división y luego 4 del lado izquierdo, y '= 8' a la derecha. ¿Qué opción coincide exactamente?

approaching.instructions: Sort each word phrase into the operation it represents.
hints: Read each phrase and think: does it mean combining, taking away, making groups, or sharing equally?
'More than' and 'sum' both mean addition. 'Less than' and 'fewer' both mean subtraction.
approaching.label: Sort each phrase into the correct operation.
approaching.explanation: Each phrase names one operation by describing what happens to the amount: 'more than', 'increased by', and 'sum of' all combine, while 'less than', 'decreased by', and 'fewer than' all take away. 'Times', 'product of', and 'twice' build equal groups, and 'divided by', 'split equally', and 'quotient of' break an amount into equal shares.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada frase nombra una operación al describir lo que le pasa a la cantidad: 'more than', 'increased by' y 'sum of' combinan, mientras que 'less than', 'decreased by' y 'fewer than' quitan. 'Times', 'product of' y 'twice' forman grupos iguales, y 'divided by', 'split equally' y 'quotient of' reparten una cantidad en partes iguales.
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada frase en la operación correcta.
hintsEs: Lee cada frase y piensa: ¿significa combinar, quitar, formar grupos o repartir en partes iguales?
'Más que' y 'suma' significan ambas adición. 'Menos que' y 'menos' significan ambas sustracción.

approaching.title: Spot the Detective's Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: Eight fewer clues than a number n leaves 5 clues.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let n be the starting number of clues.

approaching.correctWork: 'Eight fewer than a number' means you start with n and take away 8, so the equation is n − 8 = 5, not 8 − n = 5. Check: 13 − 8 = 5.
hints: Does 'eight fewer than a number' start with the 8 or with the number n?
Start with n, then subtract 8: n − 8 = 5.
approaching.explanation: The clue says eight fewer clues than n, so the starting amount is n and 8 is taken away from it, but the equation was written as 8 − n = 5 with the order flipped. Subtraction is not reversible, so the correct equation is n − 8 = 5, and 13 − 8 = 5 checks out.
approaching.explanationEs: La pista dice ocho pistas menos que n, así que la cantidad inicial es n y se le quitan 8, pero la ecuación se escribió como 8 − n = 5 con el orden invertido. La resta no se puede voltear, así que la ecuación correcta es n − 8 = 5, y 13 − 8 = 5 lo comprueba.

onLevel.label: Match each situation to its equation

pairs.situation: A detective has some cases. After getting 9 new cases, she has 22.
A suspect's age divided by 3 equals 12.
Four times the number of fingerprints equals 28.
A detective had some clues. After removing 6, she had 15 left.

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully, then match based on what the problem is asking.
hints: Underline the action in each situation: 'getting 9 new', 'divided by 3', 'four times', 'removing 6'. Each one names a single operation.
Match operations first: getting more means +, removing means −, 'times' means ×, 'divided' means /. Then check that the numbers agree too.
Try the first one: she has some cases (n) and GETS 9 more to reach 22 total. That is n plus something equals 22 — find the equation shaped that way.
onLevel.explanation: Each situation names one action on an unknown amount, and that action picks the operation: getting 9 new cases is n + 9 = 22, an age split into 3 equal parts is n / 3 = 12, four times the fingerprints is 4n = 28, and removing 6 clues is n − 6 = 15. Matching the operation first narrows each pair to a single choice.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada situación nombra una acción sobre una cantidad desconocida, y esa acción elige la operación: recibir 9 casos nuevos es n + 9 = 22, una edad dividida en 3 partes iguales es n / 3 = 12, cuatro veces las huellas es 4n = 28, y quitar 6 pistas es n − 6 = 15. Emparejar primero la operación reduce cada pareja a una sola opción.

rows.situation: A box holds some files. After removing 5, there are 13 left.
rows.variable: Number of files in the box

rows.situation: A detective split 48 photos equally into folders. Each folder has 6 photos.

onLevel.label: For each situation, identify what the variable represents and write the equation.
onLevel.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Row 1: the box starts with an unknown number of files — that unknown starting amount is exactly what n stands for.
Ask two questions for each row: What number don't we know? (that's n) What happened to it? (5 removed, or 48 photos split equally).
Row 1: removing 5 files is subtraction, and 13 remain — so write n, minus 5, equals 13. Then set up row 2 the same careful way.
onLevel.explanation: In row 1 the unknown is how many files the box started with, and removing 5 leaves 13, so n − 5 = 13. In row 2 the 48 photos are known and the unknown is how many folders they were split into, so n stands for the number of folders and the equation is 48 / n = 6.
onLevel.explanationEs: En la fila 1 lo desconocido es cuántos archivos había al principio en la caja, y al quitar 5 quedan 13, así que n − 5 = 13. En la fila 2 las 48 fotos son conocidas y lo desconocido es en cuántas carpetas se repartieron, así que n representa el número de carpetas y la ecuación es 48 / n = 6.
onLevel.labelEs: Para cada situación, identifica qué representa la variable y escribe la ecuación.
hintsEs: Fila 1: la caja empieza con un número desconocido de archivos; esa cantidad inicial desconocida es exactamente lo que representa n.
Hazte dos preguntas en cada fila: ¿qué número no conocemos? (ese es n) ¿Qué le pasó? (se quitaron 5, o se repartieron 48 fotos en partes iguales).
Fila 1: quitar 5 archivos es resta y quedan 13, así que escribe n, menos 5, igual a 13. Luego arma la fila 2 con el mismo cuidado.

onLevel.stem: A detective found some fingerprints on Monday and 14 more on Tuesday, for a total of 30. Which equation represents this?
onLevel.explanation: The detective's Monday fingerprints (f) plus 14 more equals 30: f + 14 = 30.
choiceFeedback: The 14 were found in addition to Monday's, so they are added, not subtracted.
Multiplying would mean the Monday prints were repeated 14 times over. The words say 14 more prints were found, which is about combining amounts.
Dividing splits the prints into 14 equal groups, which is not what happened on Tuesday. Reread what the detective did with the 14 new prints.
hints: Monday's fingerprints are the unknown f. On Tuesday she found 14 MORE, and the two days together total 30.
'More' means the two amounts combine into one total. Combining to reach a total is addition, not multiplying or dividing.
Write it in story order: f (Monday) plus 14 (Tuesday) equals 30 (total). Which choice shows that sum?
onLevel.stemEs: Un detective encontró algunas huellas dactilares el lunes y 14 más el martes, para un total de 30. ¿Cuál ecuación representa esto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Las huellas del lunes (f) más 14 más es igual a 30: f + 14 = 30.
hintsEs: Las huellas del lunes son la incógnita f. El martes encontró 14 MÁS, y los dos días juntos suman 30.
'Más' significa que las dos cantidades se combinan en un total. Combinar para llegar a un total es suma, no multiplicación ni división.
Escríbelo en el orden de la historia: f (lunes) más 14 (martes) es igual a 30 (total). ¿Qué opción muestra esa suma?

onLevel.label: Build the equation 2n + 3 = 11 on the balance scale and find n.
hints: The left side is 2n + 3. The right side is 11. What value of n makes both sides equal?
Try n = 4: 2(4) + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11. It balances!
onLevel.explanation: The scale balances only when the left side, 2n + 3, weighs the same as the right side, 11. Two groups of 4 plus 3 gives 8 + 3 = 11, so n = 4 makes both pans equal.
onLevel.explanationEs: La balanza se equilibra solo cuando el lado izquierdo, 2n + 3, pesa lo mismo que el lado derecho, 11. Dos grupos de 4 más 3 dan 8 + 3 = 11, así que n = 4 hace que los dos platillos queden iguales.

onLevel.title: Crack the Equation Error

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: A number of case files divided by 3 equals 6.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let n be the number of case files.

onLevel.correctWork: 'Divided by 3' means division, not multiplication. The correct equation is n / 3 = 6, not 3n = 6. Check: 18 / 3 = 6.
hints: Does 'divided by 3' tell you to multiply by 3 or split into 3 equal groups?
'A number divided by 3' is n / 3, so the equation is n / 3 = 6.
onLevel.titleEs: Descifra el error de la ecuación
onLevel.explanation: The clue says the case files are divided by 3, but the equation 3n = 6 multiplies instead. Dividing means splitting n into 3 equal groups, so the equation is n / 3 = 6, and 18 / 3 = 6 confirms it.
onLevel.explanationEs: La pista dice que los expedientes se dividen entre 3, pero la ecuación 3n = 6 multiplica en su lugar. Dividir significa repartir n en 3 grupos iguales, así que la ecuación es n / 3 = 6, y 18 / 3 = 6 lo confirma.

extending.title: Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: 'Twice' means multiply by 2, not add 2. The correct equation is 2n = 16.
hints: What does 'twice' really mean — adding or multiplying?
'Twice a number' means 2 times the number, so the equation is 2n = 16.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la ecuación
extending.explanation: The operation was named wrong at the start: 'twice' was called addition, which led to n + 2 = 16. Twice a number means two of that number, which is multiplication, so the equation is 2n = 16.
extending.explanationEs: La operación se nombró mal desde el inicio: se dijo que 'twice' era una suma, lo que llevó a n + 2 = 16. El doble de un número significa dos veces ese número, que es multiplicación, así que la ecuación es 2n = 16.

extending.prompt: Write a real-world situation that can be modeled by the equation n / 5 = 9. Explain what n represents and verify your equation makes sense.
extending.sentenceFrame: Situation: ___. In this problem, n represents ___. Check: n = ___ because ___ ÷ 5 = 9.
extending.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: n / 5 = 9 says: some amount n is split into 5 equal shares, and each share is 9. Think of things that get shared equally.
Pick a context — n stickers shared by 5 friends, n dollars split 5 ways. Say clearly what n counts, then check your value by multiplying 9 × 5.
Start your sentence: 'I had n ___ and split them equally among 5 ___; each got 9.' Then find n by computing 9 × 5 and checking it back.
extending.explanation: The equation n / 5 = 9 describes one amount being shared into 5 equal groups with 9 in each group, so a matching story could be n stickers split evenly among 5 friends with each friend getting 9. Since 5 groups of 9 rebuild the whole, n = 9 × 5 = 45, and 45 ÷ 5 = 9 checks the story.
extending.explanationEs: La ecuación n / 5 = 9 describe una cantidad que se reparte en 5 grupos iguales con 9 en cada grupo, así que una historia que encaja podría ser n calcomanías repartidas entre 5 amigos y cada uno recibe 9. Como 5 grupos de 9 reconstruyen el total, n = 9 × 5 = 45, y 45 ÷ 5 = 9 comprueba la historia.
extending.promptEs: Escribe una situación de la vida real que se pueda modelar con la ecuación n / 5 = 9. Explica qué representa n y comprueba que tu ecuación tiene sentido.
hintsEs: n / 5 = 9 dice: una cantidad n se reparte en 5 partes iguales y cada parte es 9. Piensa en cosas que se reparten por igual.
Escoge un contexto: n calcomanías repartidas entre 5 amigos, n dólares divididos en 5. Di claramente qué cuenta n y comprueba tu valor multiplicando 9 × 5.
Empieza tu oración: 'Tenía n ___ y los repartí en partes iguales entre 5 ___; a cada uno le tocaron 9.' Luego halla n calculando 9 × 5 y compruébalo.

rows.matches: Five identical bags hold 35 clues total.
rows.doesNotMatch: A detective has 5 more clues than 35.

rows.matches: After giving away 8 items, a detective has 12 left.
rows.doesNotMatch: A detective collected 8 items and then 12 more.

extending.label: For each equation, explain why one situation matches and the other does not.
extending.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Row 1: 5n = 35 means 5 EQUAL groups of n. Ask which situation really has equal groups and which one just adds more.
For each row, name the operation the equation uses (× or −), then test whether each situation's story truly uses that same operation.
Row 1: the non-match says '5 MORE clues' — 'more' signals addition, but 5n is multiplication. Explain that mismatch in your own words, then do row 2.
extending.explanation: 5n = 35 needs 5 equal groups, which the five identical bags provide; '5 more clues than 35' only adds, so it would be 35 + 5, not multiplication. In the same way n − 8 = 12 needs 8 taken away from an unknown start, which giving away 8 does; collecting 8 and then 12 more is addition, so it does not fit the equation.
extending.explanationEs: 5n = 35 necesita 5 grupos iguales, que es justo lo que dan las cinco bolsas idénticas; '5 pistas más que 35' solo suma, así que sería 35 + 5 y no una multiplicación. De la misma forma, n − 8 = 12 necesita que se quiten 8 de un inicio desconocido, que es lo que hace regalar 8; juntar 8 y luego 12 más es una suma, así que no encaja con la ecuación.
extending.labelEs: Para cada ecuación, explica por qué una situación corresponde y la otra no.
hintsEs: Fila 1: 5n = 35 significa 5 grupos IGUALES de n. Pregunta cuál situación de verdad tiene grupos iguales y cuál solo agrega más.
Para cada fila, nombra la operación que usa la ecuación (× o −) y luego prueba si la historia de cada situación realmente usa esa misma operación.
Fila 1: la que no coincide dice '5 pistas MÁS' — 'más' señala suma, pero 5n es multiplicación. Explica ese desajuste con tus palabras y luego haz la fila 2.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Write Equations is writing subtraction and division clues in the wrong order — putting the number from the clue first instead of the variable first. For 'a number decreased by 8 equals 5,' students often write 8 − n = 5 instead of the correct n − 8 = 5; for 'a number divided by 4 equals 6,' they write 4 ÷ n (or 4n) instead of n / 4 = 6. Always start with the variable, then attach the operation in the order the words describe it, and check by substituting your answer back in.

diagram.title: Stolen Paintings Part-Whole
diagram.caption: The whole bar is all 37 stolen paintings; it splits into recovered (p) and 14 still missing, so p + 14 = 37 gives p = 23.

connect.scenario: A detective is tracking stolen paintings. She knows that the number of paintings recovered plus 14 paintings still missing equals the 37 total stolen. The equation p + 14 = 37 represents this situation.
connect.promptQuestion: How many paintings has the detective recovered? How did writing an equation help you understand the situation?
connect.prompt: The detective recovered ___ paintings because p + 14 = 37 means p = 37 − ___ = ___.

choices: To keep the equation balanced while isolating p
Because subtraction is easier than addition
To make the answer a whole number
check.explanation: An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other, or the two sides stop being equal.
Substituting p = 23 back in gives 23 + 14 = 37, which is true. That confirms the solution.

connect.modelAnswer: p + 14 = 37. Subtract 14 from both sides: p = 37 − 14 = 23 paintings recovered. Check it: 23 + 14 = 37. ✓

exitTicket.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number divided by 6 equals 9'?
choiceFeedback: "Divided" means division, not multiplication.
That shows subtracting 6. The words say divided by 6.
Use division here, not addition.
hints: Find the operation phrase: 'divided by 6'. That phrase tells you the exact symbol to use.
Keep the sentence order: the number n comes first, then it is divided by 6, then 'equals 9'.
Build it piece by piece: n, then the division symbol, then 6, then '= 9'. Which choice matches that structure?
